thought.text:
Diagnosis: `_equal_sign` (`=[^\S\r\n]*`) consumes whitespace after `=`, so for `KEY= # explanation` the value part begins at `#`, and `parse_unquoted_value`'s strip regex `\s+#.*` finds no preceding whitespace — yielding `"# explanation"` instead of `""`.

Change plan (parser.py only): revert `_equal_sign` to `=` (no trailing-whitespace consumption) so the leading space stays in the value part. Then in `parse_unquoted_value`, strip a comment only when whitespace precedes `#`: use `re.sub(r"\s+#.*", "", part).rstrip()`. This keeps `KEY=#literal` → `"#literal"` and `KEY=a#b` → `"a#b"` (no preceding whitespace), while `KEY= # explanation` → `""`. Quoting, exports, and ordinary comments are unaffected since `_comment`/`_end_of_line` still handle trailing comments.
